"We've caught, for the first time, a star's final nuclear heartbeat, frozen in gas."

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

As ubiquitous as the sun is to us today, our star is not eternal; one day, albeit in billions of years, it will die. While massive stars die in supernova explosions, the sun and stars of similar mass die quieter deaths. But that doesn't mean these stars completely go out with a whimper.

New observations collected using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), the world's largest radio telescope comprised of 66 antennas in northern Chile, reveal that the sun's death throes may be different from what scientists had initially believed.

NASA Jet Propulsion Lab (JPL) researcher Raghvendra Sahai, who led the investigation, explained the shape the ALMA observations took: "It's essentially a physical snapshot of an event that, until now, we've mostly inferred from theoretical models. We've caught, for the first time, a star's final nuclear heartbeat, frozen in gas."

Sun-like stars "die" when they run out of hydrogen in their cores. This means that the fusion of hydrogen to helium ceases in the stellar core, and because this nuclear process is a star's main energy source, the star no longer has the outward push to support itself against the inward push of its own gravity.

As the star's core collapses to create a stellar remnant called a white dwarf, the outer layers where hydrogen is still fusing to form helium swell out. This expansion leads to a relatively short-lived "red giant" phase. Eventually, these outer layers will cool and disperse, leaving the central white dwarf surrounded by a so-called "planetary nebula" shell of debris.

During the red giant phase, as the stellar core is surrounded by shells of hydrogen and helium, these layers are occasionally rocked by flares in nuclear activity called thermal pulses. During these episodes, stellar material is flung into space.

To better understand this phase in stellar evolution, the team focused ALMA on a star called IRAS 06530-0213, located around 12,000 light-years away in the constellation Monoceros. This revealed a giant ring of gas that appears to be a frozen fossil of the star's last thermonuclear flare-up. This thermonuclear fossil rings an hourglass-shaped planetary nebula in the act of forming.

"Most of us think of stars as unchanging points of light, but this is a real-time snapshot of a star's death throes," Sahai said. "It's the brief, violent transition between a bloated red giant and a glowing planetary nebula, frozen mid-action."

The team was able to determine that this gas shell of IRAS 06530-0213 is around half a light-year wide and was ejected into space around 6,500 years ago. It represents the first direct evidence of the last thermal pulse before this kind of star enters the final phase of its life.

The team thinks that for around 2,000 years after the pulse, the star lost mass at a lower rate. This mass loss then increased sharply over the following 1,000 years. This led to the creation of a lumpy shell of gas now seen as a tangle of material filaments around the dying star. The fact that these filaments have a spiral shape could indicate that IRAS 06530-0213 has an unseen partner orbiting it, stirring the gas.

Meanwhile, the hourglass-shaped nebula immediately around the star began to take shape around 700 years ago, meaning that the red giant phase for IRAS 06530-0213 only ended very recently, in cosmic terms at least.

There are also unexpected elements to the ALMA observations of IRAS 06530-0213.

The team discovered an unexpected abundance of heavy versions, or isotopes, of elements like carbon, oxygen and nitrogen around IRAS 06530-0213.

This doesn't conform to models of how stars like IRAS 06530-0213 forge elements and mix them into their surroundings, though similar signatures have been seen around odd stellar objects, with violent bursts of nuclear fusion thought to be the cause.As well as seeing something unexpected, the researchers didn't detect something they expected to observe.

Dying stars like IRAS 06530-0213 have previously been known to have companions, typically sitting with them inside compact disks of dust. These disks are indirect evidence of material being dragged from the close companion star to the dying star. This is a process scientists have used to explain jet-sculpted hourglass shapes.

However, ALMA failed to detect such disk around IRAS 06530. The team suggests that this could be because a disk existed, albeit briefly, during which time it powered a short burst of high-speed jets that helped sculpt the hourglass, following this the disk simply faded away.

"Dying stars so often have hidden companions that reshape their ejected material into intricate, bipolar or multipolar forms instead of simple spheres," Sahai concluded. "IRAS 06530 shows that the story is more complicated than the tidy explanation we've been using."The team's research was published on Friday (Nov. 20) in The Astrophysical Journal.

Robert Lea is a science journalist in the U.K. whose articles have been published in Physics World, New Scientist, Astronomy Magazine, All About Space, Newsweek and ZME Science. He also writes about science communication for Elsevier and the European Journal of Physics. Rob holds a bachelor of science degree in physics and astronomy from the U.K.’s Open University. #684. Guy Fieri Debuts Shocking Gray Hair Transformation

Guy Fieri’s new, naturally gray hair stole the show on Thanksgiving, leaving many fans stunned after he debuted the look on Instagram.

Guy Fieri served up a major makeover alongside his turkey.

While the Food Network chef’s spiked, bleach blonde hair and goatee have long been his signature look, Fieri shocked fans with naturally gray hair in a Thanksgiving photo carousel.

In fact, while the 58-year-old pointed to his plate full of delicious looking food in the first slide, it was his hair that truly gobbled up fans’ attention.

“Your hair looks so good grey!!!! Dont [sic] go back to blonde,” one user wrote in the comments, while another added, “PLEASE TELL ME YOU'RE KEEPING THE GRAY HAIR!!!!”

But though Fieri’s bleached locks are now a natural shade, a second photo showing the Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives star helping himself to food revealed that his signature spikes are still firmly intact.

As for his Turkey Day celebrations, Fieri was joined by his and wife Lori Fieri’s sons Hunter Fieri and Ryder Fieri, as well as a whole other host of loved ones as they dined together in a covered pergola outside.

“Hope you all had an amazing Thanksgiving!!” Fieri captioned his Nov. 26 post, encouraging fans to “leave a comment sharing something you’re thankful for.”

Of course, those who have been staying tuned in to the chef’s journey through Flavortown over the years will know this isn’t the first time Fieri has stunned fans by cooking up a completely new look.

Back in January, Fieri shared a video to Instagram in which he’d lost both his facial hair and his blonde locks, instead appearing cleanshaven with brown hair upon his head, hair that was styled into a much more classic look than his usual.

“Hey there,” Fieri said in the Jan. 22 video clip as he stood before a lit birthday cake. “After so many years of celebrating my birthday as Guy, I thought this year I’d celebrate it as ‘just a guy.’ Happy birthday to me.”

But while the video sent shockwaves throughout the internet—with many users decrying the clip as AI—it was later revealed to be part of Fieri’s Super Bowl partnership with Bosch.

"My commitment to doing this was, 'Okay, we're playing big ball. And I'll play,’" he told Entertainment Weekly of the transformation. "What it turned out to be, what people are going to see, I'm just gonna turn my phone off for about three weeks after this, because people are gonna hammer me."

Meanwhile, his family wanted front row seats to the transformation.

“My wife said to me, 'I gotta see this,’” Fieri revealed. “‘I gotta be there for this.’”

As for how other stars celebrated Thanksgiving this year, read on.

The Nobody Wants This star took advantage of Thanksgiving to reveal she and husband Tyson Mason to announce she's pregnant with their second baby.

The Witcher alum proved it's not only his acting that is super, but also his grilling skills.

The “Honey Bee” singer and “Hollaback Girl” hitmaker snuggled in close as they expressed gratitude for their fans. As Shelton wrote on Instagram Nov. 26, “Hoping everybody has a happy Thanksgiving!!! Thankful for y'all!!!!”

The supermodel and jiu jitsu instructor showed off their model life with their 21-month-old son.

“The amount of goodness we experience in life depends on our ability to notice it," Bündchen captioned her Nov. 26 Instagram post, which also featured pictures of her and ex-husband Tom Brady's kids Benjamin, 16, and Vivian, 13. "Gratitude is contagious, and the more we can appreciate the beauty around us, the more joy we bring into our lives and the lives of others."

She added, "May we always find something to be grateful for, not just today, but every day. Happy Thanksgiving! Sending you all so much love."

It was a celebration for the girls as Dunham marked her first Thanksgiving as a mom alongside husband Luis Felber.

As she captioned the Nov. 26 Instagram post as the family went on a stroll, "Thankful."

You oughta know how excited the country music star is about the holiday season.

“Time for a little more peace, love and cowboys,” she wrote on Instagram Nov. 26. “Let the holiday shenanigans begin happy Thanksgiving from my family to y’all’s!”

The Freaky Friday star got reflective this Thanksgiving as she shared an image of herself stretching while enjoying an ocean view.

"Going to turn off the noise for a moment," she wrote on Instagram Nov. 26. "To all out there in this vast environment that we opt into, that if you're lucky enough to have one, the Thanksgiving meal is not hard. It's a roasted bird and potatoes."

"What's hard are the people with their binary and rigid ideas and judgments and petty selfishness," she added. "Today let's all be like Dolly [Parton] and be welcoming and gentle and generous."

The Red Table Talk host showed off her family's extravagant Thanksgiving set-up.

"Preparing for Thanksgiving dinner at the family abode," she wrote on Instagram Nov. 26. "Happy Day of thanks to you all and may you, your families and loved ones continue to be lifted and showered by the gifts of grace from the Highest. They may not always show up how we want them to … but they are there."

The chef cooked up more than a Thanksgiving meal—he also debuted naturally gray hair.

The actor was grateful for some one-on-one time this Thanksgiving.
